texts.orig: Weather Report
texts.text: Weather Report

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Scattered rain events brought rain throughout the province. The Southwest, Northwest, Central and the Interlake regions received less than 10 mm of precipitation with many areas receiving less than 5 mm. The largest accumulations occurred in the East region with Prawda having the highest accumulation at 38.3 mm.
texts.text: Scattered rain events brought rain throughout the province. The Southwest, Northwest, Central and the Interlake regions received less than 10 mm of precipitation with many areas receiving less than 5 mm. The largest accumulations occurred in the East region with Prawda having the highest accumulation at 38.3 mm.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Climate normals for total accumulated precipitation from May 1 to August 9 range from 191 mm to 289 mm and are based on 30-year historical data. Since May 1, areas of the Northwest and Interlake regions have accumulated 300 mm of precipitation. Seasonal accumulations are above normal for the entire Northwest and large areas of the Southwest and Interlake. Areas of the Central and Southwest region have near-normal accumulation. A few localized areas of the Southwest, Central, and Eastern regions have seen accumulations below 80% of the 30-year average.

A few localized areas of the Southwest, Central, and Eastern regions have seen accumulations below 80% of the 30-year average.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Total Accumulation of Growing Degree Days shows the accumulated growing degree days (GDD) for the period of May 1 - August 9, 2026. GDD accumulations ranged between 968 and 1339 GDD so far this growing season. Most of southern Manitoba has accumulated more than 1500 GDD.

texts.text: Harvest has started in winter cereal crops, no yield reports at this time.

texts.text: The majority of spring cereals are in the soft to hard dough stage. Desiccation has started in spring cereals, swathing of oats will likely start this week. Harvest has started in the earliest barley fields.

texts.orig: Forages
texts.text: Forages

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Forage harvest continues across the region, with producers at varying stages of first and second-cut harvest. Hay quality is generally good, with average to above-average yields reported.
texts.text: Forage harvest continues across the region, with producers at varying stages of first and second-cut harvest. Hay quality is generally good, with average to above-average yields reported.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Dairy producers in Eastern and Central Manitoba have completed second cut, with central Manitoba producers beginning third cut.
texts.text: Dairy producers in Eastern and Central Manitoba have completed second cut, with central Manitoba producers beginning third cut.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Limited recent rainfall is causing forage regrowth to be slow in some areas. Forage growth has stalled in some areas that previously had standing water and are now drying down.
texts.text: Limited recent rainfall is causing forage regrowth to be slow in some areas. Forage growth has stalled in some areas that previously had standing water and are now drying down.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Annual forage oats are performing exceptionally well and are at the mid-milk stage. Barely is also performing well, with large seed heads.
texts.text: Annual forage oats are performing exceptionally well and are at the mid-milk stage. Barely is also performing well, with large seed heads.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Cereal silage harvest is well underway, with yields expected to be above average in several areas.
texts.text: Cereal silage harvest is well underway, with yields expected to be above average in several areas.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Silage corn is progressing well and is in good condition.
texts.text: Silage corn is progressing well and is in good condition.

texts.orig: Livestock
texts.text: Livestock

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Cattle remain in generally good condition on pasture, with decent to ample forage supplies reported across much of the region. However, pasture forage supplies are diminishing and drying up in some areas. Additional rainfall would improve pasture conditions and support regrowth.
texts.text: Cattle remain in generally good condition on pasture, with decent to ample forage supplies reported across much of the region. However, pasture forage supplies are diminishing and drying up in some areas. Additional rainfall would improve pasture conditions and support regrowth.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Dugout water levels are generally still sufficient but are declining in some areas; levels are approximately 70% in areas where reported.
texts.text: Dugout water levels are generally still sufficient but are declining in some areas; levels are approximately 70% in areas where reported.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · The break in the heat wave has provided welcome relief for cattle, allowing them to spend more time grazing during the day.
texts.text: The break in the heat wave has provided welcome relief for cattle, allowing them to spend more time grazing during the day.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Foot rot continues to be a concern on pastures along with other livestock health concerns including pneumonia, pink eye, and ringworm.
texts.text: Foot rot continues to be a concern on pastures along with other livestock health concerns including pneumonia, pink eye, and ringworm.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Fly pressure remains high, while mosquito pressure has decreased with increased dragonfly activity.
texts.text: Fly pressure remains high, while mosquito pressure has decreased with increased dragonfly activity.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Producers are preparing for manure application and cleaning out winter corrals and feeding areas ahead of cattle returning from pasture.
texts.text: Producers are preparing for manure application and cleaning out winter corrals and feeding areas ahead of cattle returning from pasture.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Regional Comments
texts.text: Regional Comments

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Southwest
texts.text: Southwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Cooler temperatures this week, with daytime temperatures in the mid 20's and nighttime temperatures in the single digits. Flood-affected areas are beginning recovery efforts, and producers are preparing land for the coming year. A week of good weather helped crops ripen and brought harvest closer. Most crops are turning faster than expected.
texts.text: Cooler temperatures this week, with daytime temperatures in the mid 20's and nighttime temperatures in the single digits. Flood-affected areas are beginning recovery efforts, and producers are preparing land for the coming year. A week of good weather helped crops ripen and brought harvest closer. Most crops are turning faster than expected.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Harvest has started in fall rye. Desiccation of winter wheat has started, and harvest will begin soon in some areas. Spring cereals are ripening quickly under dry, warm conditions and some desiccation may begin by the end of the week. Barley is ripening, and some producers may start swathing soon.
texts.text: Harvest has started in fall rye. Desiccation of winter wheat has started, and harvest will begin soon in some areas. Spring cereals are ripening quickly under dry, warm conditions and some desiccation may begin by the end of the week. Barley is ripening, and some producers may start swathing soon.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Soybeans are in the R5 to early R6 stages. The crop looks promising, and additional moisture will help achieve full yield potential. Desiccation has started in pea fields, and harvest will likely begin this week.
texts.text: Soybeans are in the R5 to early R6 stages. The crop looks promising, and additional moisture will help achieve full yield potential. Desiccation has started in pea fields, and harvest will likely begin this week.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Most canola is in the pod-filling stage, and some early crops are showing slight colour change. Late-seeded fields are also moving out of flowering.
texts.text: Most canola is in the pod-filling stage, and some early crops are showing slight colour change. Late-seeded fields are also moving out of flowering.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Corn is in the blister stage (R2). Sunflowers are at approximately R5.9 to R6 stage. Early seeded flax is showing late boll colour change, while late plantings are in the green boll stage.
texts.text: Corn is in the blister stage (R2). Sunflowers are at approximately R5.9 to R6 stage. Early seeded flax is showing late boll colour change, while late plantings are in the green boll stage.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Northwest
texts.text: Northwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Milder temperatures this week along with windy conditions in the Northwest region. Soil crusting continues as soils continue to dry. Field repair and infrastructure repair continue in the region. Field access remains a challenge in some areas where washouts occurred, however many roads are becoming passable again.
texts.text: Milder temperatures this week along with windy conditions in the Northwest region. Soil crusting continues as soils continue to dry. Field repair and infrastructure repair continue in the region. Field access remains a challenge in some areas where washouts occurred, however many roads are becoming passable again.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Fall rye and winter wheat are mostly mature and harvest has started in parts of the region. Pre-harvest applications have started in winter cereals.
texts.text: Fall rye and winter wheat are mostly mature and harvest has started in parts of the region. Pre-harvest applications have started in winter cereals.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Spring cereals range from milk to soft dough stage. There are some later seeded fields that continue to catch up.
texts.text: Spring cereals range from milk to soft dough stage. There are some later seeded fields that continue to catch up.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Field peas range from the R5 to R6 stage and are moving towards maturity.
texts.text: Field peas range from the R5 to R6 stage and are moving towards maturity.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola fields continue to range in stages, with most crops in the podding stage. A few later seeded fields and fields under excess moisture continue to catch up. Fields that experienced excess moisture have patches of delayed growth.
texts.text: Canola fields continue to range in stages, with most crops in the podding stage. A few later seeded fields and fields under excess moisture continue to catch up. Fields that experienced excess moisture have patches of delayed growth.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The most advanced soybean crops have moved into R4 stage, with the remainder of the crop following behind.
texts.text: The most advanced soybean crops have moved into R4 stage, with the remainder of the crop following behind.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Central
texts.text: Central

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter wheat and fall rye fields have reached maturity and harvest has started throughout the region. No yield estimates to date. Desiccation has started on spring cereals and harvest has started on the earliest barley fields. Barley yields are reported to be very good.
texts.text: Winter wheat and fall rye fields have reached maturity and harvest has started throughout the region. No yield estimates to date. Desiccation has started on spring cereals and harvest has started on the earliest barley fields. Barley yields are reported to be very good.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Soybeans are mostly in the R5 stage (beginning seed). Harvest has started in the earliest pea fields, with more acres expected to start within the next few days.
texts.text: Soybeans are mostly in the R5 stage (beginning seed). Harvest has started in the earliest pea fields, with more acres expected to start within the next few days.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The majority of corn is in the blister (R2) to early milk stage (R3).
texts.text: The majority of corn is in the blister (R2) to early milk stage (R3).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Easly seeded canola fields are starting to change colour, later seeded fields are in the podding stage. Swathing has started in the earliest canola fields.
texts.text: Easly seeded canola fields are starting to change colour, later seeded fields are in the podding stage. Swathing has started in the earliest canola fields.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The majority of sunflowers are in full bloom, with the earliest fields at the R6 stage.
texts.text: The majority of sunflowers are in full bloom, with the earliest fields at the R6 stage.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Eastern
texts.text: Eastern

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Parts of the Eastern region received rainfall this week, with most locations receiving between 3 and 12 mm. Producers are thankful for the rain and are looking for more to help the longer season crops (corn and soybean) continue to develop and mature.
texts.text: Parts of the Eastern region received rainfall this week, with most locations receiving between 3 and 12 mm. Producers are thankful for the rain and are looking for more to help the longer season crops (corn and soybean) continue to develop and mature.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter wheat and fall rye are in the hard dough stage. Producers have desiccated fields, and harvest has started in some areas. No early yield reports have been received.
texts.text: Winter wheat and fall rye are in the hard dough stage. Producers have desiccated fields, and harvest has started in some areas. No early yield reports have been received.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: S
texts.text: S

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Manitoba The majority of spring wheat fields are in the hard dough stage. Spring wheat desiccation will begin early this week. Some barley fields have been desiccated, swathing of oats is planned for late this week. Overall, cereal crops continue to look very good.
texts.text: Manitoba The majority of spring wheat fields are in the hard dough stage. Spring wheat desiccation will begin early this week. Some barley fields have been desiccated, swathing of oats is planned for late this week. Overall, cereal crops continue to look very good.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Most corn finished the silking stage, and is now in the blister/early milk stage. The crop is continuing to grow well with all the warm temperatures and moisture we have received. Producers are hopeful that more rain will fall as kernel development is a time when high moisture is needed.
texts.text: Most corn finished the silking stage, and is now in the blister/early milk stage. The crop is continuing to grow well with all the warm temperatures and moisture we have received. Producers are hopeful that more rain will fall as kernel development is a time when high moisture is needed.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Early planted canola is beginning to change colour, with some seed colour change being noted in some fields. Later seeded or re-seeded fields have finished up flowering and are in the pod development stage. Lack of pod set during the intense heat during flowering continues to be a yield concern.
texts.text: Early planted canola is beginning to change colour, with some seed colour change being noted in some fields. Later seeded or re-seeded fields have finished up flowering and are in the pod development stage. Lack of pod set during the intense heat during flowering continues to be a yield concern.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Soybeans are at the R5 (seeds are 1/8" long at one of the top 4 nodes) stage. Overall, fields are looking good. Producers are looking for more rainfall in August to help with the pod filling stage and increase yields. Some moisture stress fields and fields planted on 30" rows are experiencing more weed pressure due to the slow closing of the canopy.
texts.text: Soybeans are at the R5 (seeds are 1/8" long at one of the top 4 nodes) stage. Overall, fields are looking good. Producers are looking for more rainfall in August to help with the pod filling stage and increase yields. Some moisture stress fields and fields planted on 30" rows are experiencing more weed pressure due to the slow closing of the canopy.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Sunflowers are in full bloom and looking good. The limited flax acres in the region have finished flowering and are turning colour.
texts.text: Sunflowers are in full bloom and looking good. The limited flax acres in the region have finished flowering and are turning colour.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Interlake
texts.text: Interlake

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Crops are maturing rapidly across the region. Field conditions have significantly improved in the southwest part of the region.
texts.text: Crops are maturing rapidly across the region. Field conditions have significantly improved in the southwest part of the region.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter wheat and fall rye have reached maturity. The majority of spring cereals are in the hard dough stage. Desiccation will start in the earliest spring wheat fields this coming week.
texts.text: Winter wheat and fall rye have reached maturity. The majority of spring cereals are in the hard dough stage. Desiccation will start in the earliest spring wheat fields this coming week.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Grain corn has had excellent growth, although some fields show variations in their development. The majority of grain corn ranges from silking to early milk stage.
texts.text: Grain corn has had excellent growth, although some fields show variations in their development. The majority of grain corn ranges from silking to early milk stage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Most pea crops are in the R5 to R6 stage. Peas are in excellent condition, with well-filled pods. Peas have been desiccated in parts of the south Interlake. Soybeans are looking very good, with the most advanced fields in the R3 to R4 stages, and some progressing into R5.
texts.text: Most pea crops are in the R5 to R6 stage. Peas are in excellent condition, with well-filled pods. Peas have been desiccated in parts of the south Interlake. Soybeans are looking very good, with the most advanced fields in the R3 to R4 stages, and some progressing into R5.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola looks excellent with strong stands and very good pod development. The earliest seeded canola fields are transitioning from full pod development to early ripening. Later seeded fields are still in the flowering stage. Sunflowers are in the R4 to R5 stage, with the earliest seeded fields approaching R5.5.
texts.text: Canola looks excellent with strong stands and very good pod development. The earliest seeded canola fields are transitioning from full pod development to early ripening. Later seeded fields are still in the flowering stage. Sunflowers are in the R4 to R5 stage, with the earliest seeded fields approaching R5.5.
